statement: Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. A frog starts at $0$ on the real axis and makes $n$ jumps of lengths $1, 2, \ldots, n$ in some order. If the frog is at $a \leq 0$ it must jump right; if at $a > 0$ it must jump left. Find the largest positive integer $k$ for which the frog can order its jumps so it never lands on any of $1, 2, \ldots, k$.
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x+y) + y \leq f(f(f(x)))$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.
